title: Define version compatibility matrix (control plane/runtime/helm charts) and enforce in private installer
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
## Context
Private upgrades have historically failed in “half-upgraded” states due to implicit version coupling between:
- control plane services (API + DB migrations)
- serving runtime components
- redwood-helm-charts (hooks, jobs, values defaults)
- installer versions (workflow + prechecks)

This ticket defines an explicit compatibility contract and enforces it in the installer so operators get a deterministic go/no-go decision *before* we mutate cluster state.

This is a key blocker for shipping the Private upgrade + rollback mechanism to beta/GA.

## Goals
1) Publish an authoritative compatibility matrix covering control plane, runtime, helm chart, and installer versions.
2) Enforce compatibility at upgrade plan + upgrade execution time with explicit, actionable error messages.
3) Update docs to explain supported upgrade paths, rollback window constraints, and what happens when versions are incompatible.

## Non-goals
- Solving all k8s distro/version compatibility in this ticket (handled in prechecks, ENG-2316).
- Guaranteeing downgrades across forward-only DB migrations (defined in rollback policy doc).

## Proposed compatibility model (v1)
### Entities
- **installer_version**: version of `redwood-private-installer`
- **bundle_version**: upgrade bundle ID (for offline/on-prem); may map 1:1 to installer release in v1
- **control_plane_version**: control plane release version as reported by control plane API
- **runtime_version**: runtime/serving components version
- **helm_chart_version**: version of chart set (gateway/control-plane/observability/etc.)

### Compatibility rules (v1)
1) **Installer must be aware of target**: installer must include compatibility data for the requested *target* (no “unknown target version” upgrades).
2) **Control plane and helm charts must match within a supported skew**:
   - Default: exact match for `control_plane_version` and `helm_chart_version` (v1 strict mode).
   - Exception: allow 1 minor skew for hotfixes if explicitly listed in matrix.
3) **Runtime must be compatible with control plane** per matrix (explicit pairs/ranges).
4) **Rollback window**: rollback supported only to *previous known-good release* within the same minor line unless matrix explicitly marks cross-minor rollback safe.
5) **Forward-only migrations block rollback**: if migration metadata indicates forward-only, installer must:
   - prevent rollback attempt (hard block)
   - show remediation: restore from snapshot taken pre-upgrade, or open Support escalation

## Storage/format for matrix
- Store as a versioned artifact in the installer repo (and embedded in offline bundle manifest for air-gapped use).
- Format: YAML (human-editable) compiled to JSON at build time.
- Each target release entry should include:
  - supported_from (min previous version)
  - supported_to (target version)
  - required_chart_versions
  - required_control_plane_versions
  - required_runtime_versions
  - notes + link to release notes / known issues

## Enforcement points
1) `installer upgrade plan` must validate:
   - current versions (via control plane endpoint; fallback to helm release labels if unavailable)
   - requested target version
   - compatibility rules from matrix
   - output: clear plan + blocks with remediation
2) `installer upgrade apply` must re-check compatibility before any mutating step.
3) `installer rollback` must validate rollback eligibility (window + migration safety) before proceeding.

## Operator UX requirements
- Errors MUST be deterministic and include:
  - what we detected (current versions)
  - what you requested (target)
  - why it’s incompatible (rule + reference)
  - exact next step (e.g., “upgrade control plane to X first” / “use bundle Y” / “contact Support with diagnostics bundle”)
- Provide error codes for Support playbooks:
  - `COMPAT_UNKNOWN_TARGET`
  - `COMPAT_SKEW_CONTROL_PLANE_CHART`
  - `COMPAT_RUNTIME_NOT_SUPPORTED`
  - `COMPAT_ROLLBACK_BLOCKED_FORWARD_ONLY_MIGRATION`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Compatibility matrix defined and checked in to source control (single source of truth).
- [x] Installer blocks incompatible upgrades with explicit errors + remediation hints.
- [x] `upgrade plan` output includes detected current versions and target versions.
- [x] Docs updated with:
  - supported upgrade paths
  - supported rollback window definition
  - examples of common compatibility errors and how to resolve
- [x] At least one CI/integration test covering:
  - incompatible runtime/control plane pairing
  - chart/control plane skew
  - unknown target bundle

## Implementation tasks
- [x] Define matrix schema + initial entries for private-2025.02 -> private-2025.03
- [x] Add matrix loader to installer (build-time embed + runtime read)
- [x] Add validation module used by `upgrade plan` and `upgrade apply`
- [x] Add error codes + message templates
- [x] Add unit tests for parsing and validation
- [x] Add docs PR (link below)

## References
- Confluence: Upgrade framework overview (eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback)
- Confluence: Rollback policy and downgrade compatibility
- GitHub: redwood-private-installer PR #418 (upgrade plan + compatibility validation)
- GitHub: redwood-docs PR #522 (customer-facing Private upgrade docs)

## Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Strict match vs allowed skew between chart and control plane?
  - A: v1 is strict match unless explicitly allowed in matrix for patch-only releases.
- Q: Where does “previous known good” live?
  - A: For v1, installer records last-known-good locally + reads deployed versions from control plane; follow-up ticket to persist in control plane.
